acceptanceCriteria.statement: "The commit row (design 1) and the WARP chip (design 2) are drawn armed on every screen but only answer a click at SYSTEM → the click does what Enter does." MEASURED: NavComputer.js:4499 wraps the _commitButtonRect test inside `if (this._levelIndex === 4)`, while navViewModes/index.js:313-322 publishes the rect at every level. The driver's `commit()` (index.js:640) already does the right thing at every level (warp to the selected/external star at 0-3; the armed _commitAction at 4).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "The selection never clears: with nothing picked, both designs frame a fallback body and say BURN TO it; picking the star leaves the frame on a planet → a real no-selection state, and a star selection that the frame follows." MEASURED: state.js:855-862 resolves D.selBody to the first habitable planet / first planet / bodies[0] when nothing is picked, and only ever to a planet or moon; designs.js:1108 (d1Ladder frame), :1810 (d2System frame), :1246-1253 (rail detail block), :1481 (d2Status), :1454 (chip `armed`) all read it as if it were a choice.

verifyVia.input: In each design at SYSTEM: (a) open with nothing selected; (b) click a planet, then click empty space; (c) click the star.
verifyVia.observable: (a) and (b): no selection frame on any body, the detail block / status line says no body is selected, the commit row / chip is drawn unarmed and Enter does nothing. (c): the frame sits on the star, the detail names the star, the commit arms for the star. D.selBody is null in (a)/(b) and a star row in (c); no painter throws on null (PanelHost freeze guard).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "The 2D maps outrun the pointer when dragged: 1.35× in design 1, 1.4× and 2.6× in design 2 → scale by the drawn map." MEASURED (arithmetic, then live): NavComputer.js:4364 scales the pan by `_viewSize / navMapSize(w,h)` = 160 texels at 417x240, while design 1 draws a 216-texel square, design 2 a 224-texel block at 1-2 and a 417-wide band at 0 (S.mapProj publishes the drawn extent).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "A drag that starts on the rail, the tabs, the status line or the commit row still pans or rotates the map → only a press on the map starts a gesture." MEASURED: NavComputer.js:4396-4411 arms every drag on any press; no region is consulted. verifyVia.input: In each design at every level, press on the rail / status row / hint row / tab strip / commit row / top bar and drag 40 texels; then press on the map and drag 40 texels.
verifyVia.observable: The chrome press moves nothing (no pan, no rotation, no ladder scroll, camera and view unchanged); the map press moves the picture as today. The y-gauge and the ladder counter still grab. Legacy still drags from anywhere.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "Right-click 'go back' is dead in every look → bind it properly." MEASURED: NavComputer.js:334 registers only a 'click' listener, :336 preventDefaults contextmenu, :4488 tests e.button === 2 inside _handleClick — browsers fire no 'click' for the secondary button, so handleEscape (:1441) is unreachable from a real mouse in all three looks.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "Under the designs the × close button is off-screen and the backdrop cannot be clicked → fix the CSS." MEASURED: style.css:1232 puts .overlay-close at top:-40px on a panel that .nav-lowres makes 100vw × 100vh (style.css:1273), so the button is above the viewport and the 20px backdrop band is gone; legacy's × is already half-clipped by the same rule on its calc(100vh - 40px) panel.
